_note: The application's own prompt fragments, as opposed to the model's.
model-prompts.json carries the instruction a model was TRAINED on, which is
the model card's wording and must not be improvised. This file carries the
wording BetterTranslator adds around it: the heading over retrieved material
when the Memory chip is attached, and the lead-in for the standing
instruction from the Advanced panel.
These were hardcoded in C# until they were moved here. They are prompt text,
they change what the model does, and someone tuning output should be able to
reach them without a compiler.
engineSystem       the engine's own translator instruction, for a model
that publishes no trained prompt of its own. Ported
verbatim from Get-TranslationSystemPrompt in
scripts\console.ps1. {TARGET} is substituted.
Its last sentence is load-bearing: it is the only place
the model is told what a [[7]] protected block is, and
without it the markup guard hides spans the model has
no idea it must reproduce.
memoryHeading      goes above the retrieved passages and the chat pairs.
It has to say the material is reference and not the text
to translate, because the instruction it sits above ends
'translate the following text' - measured: without that
sentence the model translated the heading itself.
instructionLeadIn  prefixes the standing instruction from Advanced.
memoryHeading and instructionLeadIn are inserted BEFORE the translator
instruction, never between it and the text. Placed after it, the model
translated the inserted block instead of using it.

fragments.label: Engine system prompt
fragments.text: You are a professional translator. Translate the user's text into {TARGET}. Reply with the translation only: no commentary, no quotes, no explanations. Never return the source text unchanged. Preserve formatting, line breaks, placeholders such as {name} or %s, and any markup. Tokens of the form [[7]] are protected blocks: reproduce each exactly once, in the same order, and never translate or renumber them.

fragments.label: Memory heading
fragments.text: Here is how this project has translated related wording before. Follow its terminology where it applies. It is reference, not the text to translate.
